hero.title: Study Law in Switzerland
hero.subtitle: Switzerland provides an international learning environment for students interested in law, business regulations, human rights and international relations. Its universities offer the chance to study legal systems, corporate law and international legal issues.

faq.question: What is the duration of the Law course in Switzerland?
faq.answer: Typically, a bachelor’s degree takes about 3 years and a master’s degree about 1-2 years, depending on the institution.

faq.question: How much do you pay for studying law in Switzerland?
faq.answer: The estimated annual tuition and living expenses for students are around ₹12 lakh to ₹30 lakh or more depending on the university and city.

faq.question: Is it possible for Indian students to study Law in Switzerland after Class 12?
faq.answer: Yes, provided that the university accepts Indian qualifications and there are no other academic or language requirements.

faq.question: Do I need IELTS for Law in Switzerland?
faq.answer: Not all the time. The requirements depend on the language of instruction of the program and the university’s admission policy.

faq.question: I have studied in Switzerland, can I practice law in India?
faq.answer: No, not by default. The foreign law qualifications and professional eligibility need to be examined under the applicable Indian rules. Law in Switzerland for Indian Students is an option worth exploring for applicants interested in international legal education.
